newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Eurobourses hold gains, dlr rebounds midday.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Eurobourses hold gains, dlr rebounds midday.

text.p: European stock markets held most gains at Wednesday's midsession, with France's CAC-40 index still strong after rising more than two percent to a record high.

In currency markets, the dollar steadied just below 114 yen, recovering more than half its losses overnight after the Bank of Japan's quarterly tankan survey showed large manufacturers growing surprisingly optimistic in June.

News that Compagnie Bancaire offered to buy out its units Cardif CDF.PA and Locabail for a maximum three billion francs ($515 million) helped the blue chip CAC-40 index extend initial gains made in line with Wall Street's strong close on Tuesday.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average surged 153.80 points overnight to close at 7,758.06, the third largest gain in points terms this year as worries faded that Japanese investors would sell their U.S. assets.
Cie Bancaire's offer marks its move from a holding company to an operational company, said the head of equities sales at a large French brokerage firm.
Cie Bancaire, majority-owned by financial group Paribas, said the offers were aimed at increasing its profitability.
Banking stocks jumped on the back of Cie Bancaire's nearly 7.5-percent gain, traders said.

London's FTSE-100 index held close to its session high, shrugging off a wider than expected trade gap. April's global trade deficit was 961 million pounds ($1.6 billion), up sharply from forecasts of 625 million pounds and the previous month's 671 million. May's non-European Union trade deficit was 563 million.

"It's premature to herald this as being the start of the deterioration of the trade balance, but there are definite signs of weakness in export volumes growth at the moment," said Dharshini David at HSBC Markets.
The British government debt auction of two billion pounds matched analysts' expectations and lent support to London stocks.
But the FTSE's rise was expected to remain restrained before the first budget of Britain's new Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown on July 2.
"Until we get rid of the clouds surrounding Gordon Brown's maiden budget, we'll not make any great progress," said NatWest equity strategist David McBain.
Germany's DAX index was firm, but its record high at 3,798.94 reached on June 20 remained elusive.

In currency markets, the dollar steadied after falling overnight after the Japanese central bank's June diffusion index for big manufacturers, a key gauge of business confidence, rose to plus seven from plus two in March and compared with analysts' forecasts for a fall of 0.5.
The dollar shed a yen overnight on the report, but analysts said losses were limited because optimism slipped among smaller firms to minus seven in June from minus six in March.
"The headline number may say one thing, but the underlying numbers point to the fact that the domestic economy remains depressed," said Lee Ferridge, Commerzbank currency strategist.
CURRENCIES AT 1120 GMT
The dollar was at 113.82 yen and 1.7233 marks, compared with 114.75 yen and 1.7235 marks in late European trade on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1120 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 41.2 points at 4,637.50.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 65.58 points at 2,85034.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 32.24 points at 3,788.06.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at 1030 GMT at $338.70 against $338.90 at Tuesday's close. ($ = 5.824 French Francs) ($ = 0.599 British Pounds)
